# PocketOne

> PocketOne is a community fork of PocketBase (one Go binary: database, auth, files, realtime, admin UI) with extensions for point-in-time recovery, backups, mail, many instances on one server, deploys, tokens and OAuth, MCP, and server-rendered pages.

PocketOne takes the same commands and flags as PocketBase, plus its own; core PocketBase topics live at https://pocketbase.io/docs. Agent Skills for PocketOne: https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/tree/main/agent (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add pocketonehq/pocketone`).

Every page below in one file: https://pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt

## Get started

- [What is PocketOne?](https://pocketone.dev/docs/overview): PocketOne is a community fork of PocketBase. Its core changes are kept small; everything else is an extension.
- [Installation](https://pocketone.dev/docs/installation): Install PocketOne on macOS, Windows or Linux with Homebrew, Scoop or the install script, run it, and keep it up to date.
- [Running PocketOne](https://pocketone.dev/docs/running): Your whole backend in one file - how to start it, the folders an app is made of, what superusers are, how your app's users differ, and where everything lives.
- [Coming from PocketBase](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketbase): PocketOne is PocketBase with more built in. What stays the same, and how each added feature compares.
- [LLM skills for coding agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/agents): Teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding agents PocketOne and Pages with our Agent Skills and llms.txt.

## Database

- [Collections and fields](https://pocketone.dev/docs/collections): Collections are your app's tables - base, auth and view collections, every field type and its options, and how to create and change them in the dashboard, in a migration or from code.
- [Records](https://pocketone.dev/docs/records): Find, create, change and delete records from your own code - filters with parameters, sorting and paging, reading typed values, expanding relations, transactions and raw SQL.
- [API rules and filters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/api-rules): Decide who can list, view, create, update and delete each collection's records with API rules, written in the same filter language clients use to search - with the request, auth and other collections in reach.
- [Migrations](https://pocketone.dev/docs/migrations): Migrations carry your collection changes and seed data with your code - automigrate writes them when you change collections in the dashboard, deploys apply them, and you can write your own in TypeScript or Go.
- [Key-Value Store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/kv): $kv keeps your app's settings and small pieces of state as named JSON values: no collection, no migration, and they ride along in backups.

## Users and sign-in

- [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/authentication): Sign users in with a password, a one-time code or an OAuth2 provider, add multi-factor auth, verify emails and reset passwords, and use the signed-in user in your rules and code.
- [API tokens and OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/tokens): Give a script, a CI job or a service its own long-lived token, limited to what it needs, and revoke it whenever you like. Apps and tools can also sign in to get one.

## Hooks and routes

- [Hooks](https://pocketone.dev/docs/hooks): Run your own code when something happens in your app - before or after a record is saved, on an API request, when mail is sent, when the app starts. The hook model, written in TypeScript or Go.
- [Custom routes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/routes): Add your own API endpoints to your app - path parameters, request bodies, JSON and HTML answers, auth requirements, middleware and errors - in TypeScript or Go.
- [QuickJS: the JS engine](https://pocketone.dev/docs/quickjs): PocketOne runs pb_hooks on QuickJS, a drop-in replacement for PocketBase's JS engine that adds imports, TypeScript, async handlers, shared globals and hard memory and time limits.
- [WASM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm): Bring your own WASM: call code written in Go, Rust, C or Zig from your page code, for libraries JavaScript doesn't have and work JavaScript does too slowly.

## Websites

- [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages): No-build, server-rendered multi-page apps for PocketOne. Pages is built into the pocketone binary as the pages extension.

## Email

- [Bulk mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/bulk-mail): Send a newsletter or announcement to your app's own users, from the dashboard, your terminal or an agent.

## AI

- [AI in your app](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm): $llm gives your pages and Go code cloud models: text, pictures, speech, transcription, music, video and embeddings, from Vultr, Cloudflare, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible API, on your own keys.
- [MCP for AI agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/mcp): Connect Claude or another MCP client to your app, sign in once, and let it work with your data and settings with exactly your rights.

## Deploy and run

- [Configuration](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketone-yaml): Put your app's settings in one file instead of a line of flags, keep secrets in a .env beside it, and set any extension's options.
- [Deploy and live sync](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/deploy): Send your app's hooks, migrations, pages and public files to a running PocketOne app with one command, and keep a folder in step while you work.
- [Remote CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/remote): Manage any PocketOne app from your terminal, a script or an agent. Every extension API is a command, a REST endpoint and an MCP tool at once.
- [Run on a Linux server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/guides/linux-server): Install PocketOne on a Linux server as a .deb, .rpm or .apk package, run it as a systemd service with its own HTTPS or behind a proxy, deploy your app, upgrade and uninstall.
- [Backups and restore](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/restore): Put your app's data back as it was at any moment in the last few days, from the dashboard, your terminal or an agent.
- [Many apps on one server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/isolates): Run hundreds of PocketBase apps as isolates inside one pocketone process, routed by hostname. Each starts on its first request in tens of milliseconds, costs a few MB, and is sandboxed from the others.
- [Desktop apps](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop): Turn your PocketOne app into a native desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux: the same folder you serve, one executable per platform, built from any machine with Docker.

## How-to guides

- [Starter kits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters): The Pages starter kits - from a one-page site to sign-in, realtime, a docs site and an ask-your-docs app - and how to start an app from one.
- [Example apps](https://pocketone.dev/docs/examples): PocketOne apps you can try live and read end to end - Bedtime Story and the Pages starter kits - what each does and how it's built.
- [Update pages live with htmx](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/htmx): Use HTMX with Pages: route organization, HTML fragments without layouts, shared partials, forms, and realtime updates.
- [Use a custom domain](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/custom-domain-fly-cloudflare): Step-by-step process to configure DNS records, SSL certificates, and domain verification between Fly.io and Cloudflare. Includes specific settings for A/AAAA records, CNAME verification, and SSL/TLS encryption modes.
- [Let users sign in with Google](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/google-oauth2): Set up Google OAuth2 sign-in for a PocketOne app with the auth plugin.
- [Send email through Amazon SES](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/ses): Step-by-step configuration of AWS Simple Email Service (SES) with Google Suite, including DNS records, DKIM setup, SMTP credentials, and PocketBase integration for production email delivery.

## Reference

- [JavaScript API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/javascript): The whole JavaScript API of pb_hooks and page code: what core gives every app ($app, the hooks, the classes and every type) and what each extension adds, generated from the TypeScript declarations.
- [Go API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go): The Go packages extensions and custom PocketOne builds program against: every contract's interface and types, and the helpers they share.
- [REST API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest): Every PocketOne app serves a REST API for its records, sign-in, files and realtime, plus admin endpoints for superusers. The base URL, auth header, errors, and the query parameters every list takes.
- [CLI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/cli): Every command of the pocketone binary: PocketBase's own, the standard extensions', and one per contract operation.
- [MCP tools](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/mcp): Every MCP tool a PocketOne app's contracts add at /mcp, with its token scope and arguments.
- [pocketone.yaml](https://pocketone.dev/docs/config-reference): Every section of the pocketone.yaml config file, generated from the pocketone binary.

## Extensions

- [Overview](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions): What a PocketOne extension is and how extensions work: kinds, settings, contracts, extension APIs and JavaScript.
- [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts): Every contract in PocketOne: what it promises and which extensions provide, require and work with it.
- [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/how-pocketone-fits-together): How PocketOne extensions work together: every extension API is a named, versioned contract that any extension can provide.
- [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension): How to write a PocketOne extension.

## Contracts: By name

- [api-tokens.verify/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens.verify/v1): Another server checks an app's API token: who it acts as and what it may do.
- [api-tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/api-tokens/v1): An app's API tokens: check one, register scopes, read a request's token, limit in-process requests; the token API.
- [bulkmail/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1): Run bulk mail campaigns: count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign.
- [cache.clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache.clear/v1): Emptying an app's cache buckets, one or all, from the dashboard, the CLI or an agent.
- [cache/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cache/v1): Named buckets of bytes an app keeps for a while, with limits and eviction; memory, disk or a shared cache behind it.
- [cli.commands/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cli.commands/v1): The pocketone command tree: every contract operation as a remote command by default; extensions replace or add commands.
- [deploy/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/deploy/v1): A project's code files on an app: check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree.
- [gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1): What admits requests on a multisite host: peer checks, client IPs and rate limits, in order.
- [http.wrap/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/http.wrap/v1): Middleware around everything a multisite host serves, nested in order.
- [instance.fs/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.fs/v1): An instance's code files on disk: its folder, a cache folder, one writers' lock and a restart around a change.
- [instance.lookup/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.lookup/v1): A multisite host asks what a hostname it doesn't know serves.
- [instance.resolve/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.resolve/v1): On a control plane: what a hostname serves for an edge, and the records the answer was built from.
- [instance.source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1): The instance record a multisite host serves, and where the records come from.
- [instance.tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.tokens/v1): A multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued, to accept it on the routes it answers.
- [instance.watch/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.watch/v1): An edge follows a control plane lazily: one stream, hostnames watched as requests name them.
- [kv/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/kv/v1): An app's key-value store: named JSON values with no collection or migration, kept in PocketBase's _params.
- [llm.align/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.align/v1): Forced alignment: audio and the exact words spoken in it in, the time of every line and word out.
- [llm.chat/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.chat/v1): Stored conversations with a language model: start a chat, send to it, read its history, find and forget chats by the app's own meta.
- [llm.embed/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.embed/v1): Turn texts into vectors for search by meaning: texts in, one vector each out.
- [llm.image/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.image/v1): Make pictures from a prompt, or change pictures you give it; they come back as files.
- [llm.ledger/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.ledger/v1): What an app's model calls used and cost, from the ledger every llm.* call leaves, and how much of each limit is left.
- [llm.music/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.music/v1): Make music from a prompt and lyrics, as a job: start it, follow it, fetch its files (or wait for them).
- [llm.search/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.search/v1): RAG knowledge bases (buckets) with hybrid search: sources (files, folders, zips, pages, Git repositories, collections) kept current, one embedding model per app.
- [llm.speech/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.speech/v1): Read text aloud: text in, an audio file out, in a voice the model offers.
- [llm.text/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.text/v1): Ask a language model: a prompt or a conversation in, text (or JSON matching a schema) out, whole or streamed.
- [llm.transcribe/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.transcribe/v1): Write down what's said in audio: an audio file in, text out.
- [llm.video/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/llm.video/v1): Make video from a prompt (and a first frame), as a job: start it, follow it, fetch its files (or wait for them).
- [mail.fallback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.fallback/v1): Where an app's mail goes when SMTP is off: a chain of providers that send it or pass it on.
- [mail.feedback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1): Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on.
- [mail.suppression/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1): Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries.
- [mcp/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mcp/v1): The app's MCP endpoint at /mcp, with every provided contract's operations as tools.
- [oauth/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/oauth/v1): The app's OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the CLI and MCP clients can sign in.
- [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1): Remote control of an app: whoami, status, restart, logs. The base every client starts from.
- [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1): Put an app's data back as it was at a moment: from continuous history, or the latest backup before it.
- [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1): What runs a multisite host's instances (as isolates, in containers): one per host.
- [settings/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/settings/v1): The settings an app's admins change for its extensions, one API for all of them.
- [templates/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/templates/v1): An extension's own pages as Go templates a project can eject and edit.
- [tls/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tls/v1): The TLS of a multisite host's listener: automatic certificates instead of certificate files.
- [vacuum/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/vacuum/v1): Compacting an app's databases so freed space goes back to the disk, and when it last happened.

## Desktop: How it works

- [How the app runs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/runtime): What a PocketOne desktop app does on your users' machines: where their data lives, how upgrades migrate it, the window, and what each platform needs.

## Desktop: Guides

- [Building](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/build): pocketone desktop build: which platforms, the Docker build image, building with your own Go, and what lands in dist/.
- [Signing and sharing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/signing): Sign your PocketOne desktop app so people can install it without warnings: Developer ID signing and notarization on macOS, Authenticode on Windows, checksums and signatures on Linux.

## Extensions

- [All extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/all): Every extension in PocketOne, grouped by what it's for.
- [Extension APIs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/apis): Every contract API of a PocketOne app with its standard extensions: method, path, token scope and input.

## Extensions: Standard extensions

- [API Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens): Long-lived API tokens with scopes.
- [API Tokens: OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/api-tokens/oauth): API Tokens: OAuth
- [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls): Certificates on demand and wildcards through ACME.
- [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups): Restore an app to a moment from its own backups: the latest one before it. On by default.
- [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail): Campaigns to your app's own users, with audiences from a collection, a view or SQL.
- [Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/cache): Cache buckets for every app in the process from one shared store: bytes or Go values, a budget per bucket, LRU/MRU/FIFO/LIFO eviction, TTLs, a cold disk tier that keeps identical values once.
- [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config): The pocketone.yaml config file, with secrets in a .env beside it.
- [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy): pocketone deploy, dev, pull and logs, and the deploy API.
- [Desktop](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/desktop/extension): Build your PocketOne app into a native desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux, one executable each, from any machine.
- [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm): PocketOne's JS engine: one QuickJS VM per app, real globals, async handlers, hard limits.
- [Key-Value Store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/kv/extension): Named JSON values for an app's settings and state, with no collection or migration. On by default.
- [LLM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/extension): Cloud models for your app: text, pictures, speech, transcription, alignment, music, video and embeddings from Vultr, Cloudflare, OpenRouter or any OpenAI-compatible API.
- [LLM Chat](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-chat): Stored conversations with a language model: $llm.chat.open(id).sendAsync(text), with history and summaries.
- [LLM Search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm-search): RAG and hybrid search: knowledge bases (buckets) of files, folders, zips, web pages, Git repositories and collections; $llm.search, and enrich to ground $llm calls in them.
- [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp): An MCP endpoint at /mcp so agents can manage your app and call its tools.
- [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/extension): Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder.
- [Pages: Pages specification](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/spec): Pages: Pages specification
- [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr): Point-in-time restore of your database with Litestream. On by default.
- [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes): Named remotes and saved logins for the pocketone command.
- [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback): A default bucket for uploads and backups when an instance has no S3 of its own.
- [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect): File downloads as short-lived signed S3 redirects.
- [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings): One API for the settings an app's admins change for its extensions. On by default.
- [Templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/templates): Theme an extension's own pages (the OAuth sign-in screens): eject its templates to pb_templates and edit them.
- [UI Cache](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/uicache): Dashboard cache headers that let updates through browsers and CDNs. On by default.
- [Upgrade](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/upgrade): pocketone upgrade to the latest release, keeping the old executable.
- [Vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum): Compact your app's SQLite databases on a schedule, so space freed by deleted records goes back to the disk.
- [WASM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/extension): Bring your own WASM: Go, Rust or Zig modules called from page code, each a closed box.

## Extensions: Run many instances

- [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker): A host provider that runs each instance in its own container.
- [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge): Forwards each request to the edge that owns the instance.
- [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall): Peer allow-lists, trusted proxies and rate limits for a host.
- [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership): A control plane and its edges, across regions.
- [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite): Many instances behind one listener, routed by hostname, run by one provider.
- [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker): Hundreds of PocketBase instances in one Go process, routed by hostname.
- [Pocker: Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker): Pocker: Pocker
- [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox): Confines untrusted JS hooks, SQL and outbound network.
- [Schedules](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/schedules): Planned. Scheduled webhooks that wake sleeping instances.
- [Stats](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/stats): Measures disk use and last request for each instance a host serves.

## Extensions: Services for your instances

- [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay): Outgoing mail for instances without SMTP, through your relay, with limits.
- [Server Timing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming): Server-Timing headers for each step of a request.

## Extensions: Sell it as a service

- [Lemon Squeezy Adapter](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenant-billing-ls): Planned. Lemon Squeezy as the billing provider.
- [Multitenant](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants): Planned. Accounts that own instances: quotas, owner logins, tokens and an API.
- [Multitenant Billing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenant-billing): Planned. Plans, quotas and the billing provider hook for Multitenant.

## Extensions: For extension authors

- [Bundle](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bundle): An app's hooks, migrations and public files embedded in the binary.
- [Contracts](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/README.md)
- [Dev Users](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go)
- [Extension Kit](https://github.com/pocketonehq/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/extkit.go)
- [Mail Trap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap): Dev mode: mail from an app without SMTP lands in a built-in inbox.
- [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard): The extensions every PocketOne app has, as one set a host configures.

## Go API: PocketBase

- [pocketbase](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase)
- [apis](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/apis)
- [core](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core): Package core is the backbone of PocketBase.
- [core: Records and collections](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core/records): The Records and collections types of PocketBase's Go package core.
- [core: Fields](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core/fields): The Fields types of PocketBase's Go package core.
- [core: Events](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core/events): The Events types of PocketBase's Go package core.
- [core: Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core/settings): The Settings types of PocketBase's Go package core.
- [core/validators](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/core/validators): Package validators implements some common custom PocketBase validators.
- [forms](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/forms)
- [mails](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/mails): Package mails implements various helper methods for sending common emails like forgotten password, verification, etc.
- [plugins/ghupdate](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/plugins/ghupdate): Package ghupdate implements a new command to selfupdate the current PocketBase executable with the latest GitHub release.
- [plugins/migratecmd](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/plugins/migratecmd): Package migratecmd adds a new "migrate" command support to a PocketBase instance.
- [plugins/update](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/plugins/update): Package update implements a new command to replace the current PocketBase executable with the one from the latest BugStage releases.
- [tests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tests): Package tests provides common helpers and mocks used in PocketBase application tests.
- [tools/archive](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/archive)
- [tools/auth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/auth)
- [tools/cron](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/cron): Package cron implements a crontab-like service to execute and schedule repeative tasks/jobs.
- [tools/dbutils](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/dbutils)
- [tools/filesystem](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/filesystem)
- [tools/filesystem/blob](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/filesystem/blob): Package blob defines a lightweight abstration for interacting with various storage services (local filesystem, S3, etc.).
- [tools/hook](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/hook)
- [tools/inflector](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/inflector)
- [tools/list](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/list)
- [tools/logger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/logger)
- [tools/mailer](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/mailer)
- [tools/osutils](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/osutils)
- [tools/picker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/picker)
- [tools/router](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/router)
- [tools/routine](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/routine)
- [tools/search](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/search)
- [tools/security](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/security)
- [tools/store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/store)
- [tools/subscriptions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/subscriptions)
- [tools/template](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/template): Package template is a thin wrapper around the standard html/template and text/template packages that implements a convenient registry to load and cache templates on the fly concurrently.
- [tools/tokenizer](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/tokenizer): Package tokenizer implements a rudimentary tokens parser of buffered io.Reader while respecting quotes and parenthesis boundaries.
- [tools/types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/pocketbase/tools/types): Package types implements some commonly used db serializable types like datetime, json, etc.

## Go API: Contracts

- [api-tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/api-tokens/v1): Package apitokensv1 is the api-tokens/v1 contract: an app's API tokens.
- [api-tokens/verify/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/api-tokens/verify/v1): Package verifyv1 is the api-tokens.verify/v1 contract: another server checks an app's API token.
- [bulkmail/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/bulkmail/v1): Package bulkmailv1 is the bulkmail/v1 contract: campaigns to many recipients, sent at a safe pace.
- [cache/clear/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/cache/clear/v1): Package clearv1 is the cache.clear/v1 contract: empty an app's cache buckets from outside the app's code, so its admins (the dashboard, `pocketone remote cache clear`, an agent) can drop what cache/v1 keeps for it after a change that left stale entries behind.
- [cache/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/cache/v1): Package cachev1 is the cache/v1 contract: named buckets of bytes an app keeps for a while, so extensions and apps can remember what was expensive to compute.
- [cli/commands/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/cli/commands/v1): Package clicmdv1 is the cli.commands/v1 contract: the `pocketone` command tree.
- [deploy/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/deploy/v1): Package deployv1 is the deploy/v1 contract: a project's code files on an app (check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree).
- [gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/gate/v1): Package gatev1 is the gate/v1 contract: what admits requests on a multisite host, before an instance is served or forwarded (a firewall: peer allow lists, client IPs, rate limits).
- [http/wrap/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/http/wrap/v1): Package wrapv1 is the http.wrap/v1 contract: middleware around everything a multisite host serves (a Server-Timing header, request logging).
- [instance/fs/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/fs/v1): Package fsv1 is the instance.fs/v1 contract: one instance's code files on local disk, for extensions that read and write them (ext/deploy today).
- [instance/lookup/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/lookup/v1): Package lookupv1 is the instance.lookup/v1 contract: a multisite host asks for a hostname it doesn't know.
- [instance/resolve/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/resolve/v1): Package resolvev1 is the instance.resolve/v1 contract: on a control plane (a mothership), what a hostname serves for a given edge, built from the control plane's own records, and which records each answer was built from.
- [instance/source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/source/v1): Package sourcev1 is the instance.source/v1 contract: the instance record a multisite host serves (its id, hostnames, version, folder, secrets, limits, ...) and where the records come from.
- [instance/source/v1/sourcetest](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/source/v1/sourcetest): Package sourcetest is an instance.source/v1 provider for tests: a fixed list of instances that a test can change while it runs, the way an edit to a host's instances file or a control plane's update would.
- [instance/tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/tokens/v1): Package tokensv1 is the instance.tokens/v1 contract: a multisite host checks an API token one of its instances issued, so it can accept the instance's own tokens on the routes it answers for that instance (deploy/v1, remote/v1).
- [instance/watch/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/instance/watch/v1): Package watchv1 is the instance.watch/v1 contract: an edge follows a control plane (a mothership) lazily.
- [kv/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/kv/v1): Package kvv1 is the kv/v1 contract: an app's key-value store.
- [llm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm): Package llm holds what the llm.* contracts share: a model reference, generated files, usage, model info, jobs and errors.
- [llm/align/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/align/v1): Package alignv1 is the llm.align/v1 contract: forced alignment.
- [llm/chat/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/chat/v1): Package chatv1 is the llm.chat/v1 contract: stored conversations with the app's language model.
- [llm/embed/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/embed/v1): Package embedv1 is the llm.embed/v1 contract: a model turns texts into vectors, for search by meaning.
- [llm/image/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/image/v1): Package imagev1 is the llm.image/v1 contract: a model makes pictures from a prompt, or changes pictures it's given.
- [llm/ledger/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/ledger/v1): Package ledgerv1 is the llm.ledger/v1 contract: what an app's model calls have used and cost, read from the ledger every llm.* call leaves (the provider's own record of each call), and how much of each limit is left.
- [llm/music/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/music/v1): Package musicv1 is the llm.music/v1 contract: a model makes music from a prompt (and lyrics).
- [llm/search/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/search/v1): Package searchv1 is the llm.search/v1 contract: named buckets of content an app searches.
- [llm/speech/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/speech/v1): Package speechv1 is the llm.speech/v1 contract: a model reads text aloud.
- [llm/text/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/text/v1): Package textv1 is the llm.text/v1 contract: a language model answers a prompt or a conversation.
- [llm/transcribe/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/transcribe/v1): Package transcribev1 is the llm.transcribe/v1 contract: a model writes down what's said in audio.
- [llm/video/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/llm/video/v1): Package videov1 is the llm.video/v1 contract: a model makes a video from a prompt (and a first frame).
- [mail/fallback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/mail/fallback/v1): Package fallbackv1 is the mail.fallback/v1 contract: where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off.
- [mail/feedback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/mail/feedback/v1): Package feedbackv1 is the mail.feedback/v1 contract: what mail providers report back about mail an app sent (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes), received at one place and turned into [Event]s that any extension can act on.
- [mail/suppression/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/mail/suppression/v1): Package suppressionv1 is the mail.suppression/v1 contract: addresses an app must not send bulk mail to (unsubscribed, bounced, complained), and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries.
- [mcp/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/mcp/v1): Package mcpv1 is the mcp/v1 contract: the app's Model Context Protocol endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it.
- [oauth/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/oauth/v1): Package oauthv1 is the oauth/v1 contract: an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app (authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, dynamic and metadata-document client registration), so the CLI and MCP clients like Claude can sign in.
- [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/remote/v1): Package remotev1 is the remote/v1 contract: remote control of an app.
- [remote/v1/remoteclient](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/remote/v1/remoteclient): Package remoteclient is remote/v1's CLI client: the remotes a project links (.pocketone/remotes.yaml), saved logins, sign-in (an API token, a password, or OAuth in the browser or with a device code), and an authenticated HTTP client for a remote.
- [restore/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/restore/v1): Package restorev1 is the restore/v1 contract: put an app's data back as it was at a moment.
- [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/runtime/v1): Package runtimev1 is the runtime/v1 contract: what runs a multisite host's instances (ext/pocker as isolates, ext/docker in containers).
- [settings/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/settings/v1): Package settingsv1 is the settings/v1 contract: the settings an app's admins change for its extensions (pitr's S3 bucket, bulkmail's sending limits), one API for all of them.
- [templates/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/templates/v1): Package templatesv1 is the templates/v1 contract: an extension's own pages as a set of Go html/template files that a project can override.
- [tls/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/tls/v1): Package tlsv1 is the tls/v1 contract: the TLS of a multisite host's main listener (automatic certificates).
- [vacuum/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/reference/go/vacuum/v1): Package vacuumv1 is the vacuum/v1 contract: an app's databases are compacted (SQLite VACUUM) so space freed by deleted records goes back to the disk, and its admins can see when that last happened.

## LLM: How it works

- [Search and RAG](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/search): Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and hybrid search over your own content: knowledge bases (buckets) filled from files, web pages, Git repositories and collections, and enrich to ground any $llm call in them.
- [Limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/limits): Cap what your app spends on models: limits in Settings → LLM for the whole app, each user, each guest and all guests together, by dollars, tokens or calls, per UTC day or month.
- [Users and guests](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/users-and-guests): $llm.for(ctx) counts a page's model calls for its signed-in user or its guest, so per-user and per-guest limits apply; how guests are told apart, and how to handle a refused call.
- [Spend and the ledger](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/spend): Every model call is recorded: $llm.ledger tells you what's left of each limit, what a user or guest has spent, and where the money goes, by model, kind, person or day.

## LLM: Guides

- [Structured answers](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/structured): Give $llm.text a JSON schema and get back data you can store.
- [Streaming answers](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/streaming): Show an answer as the model writes it: $llm.text.streamAsync in a page, forwarded to the browser with ctx.res.sse().
- [Pictures, speech and music](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/media): Generate pictures, narration, music and video with $llm and save them on your records as files.
- [Conversations](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/conversations): Chats that remember: send the conversation with each call, or let LLM Chat store it, summarize it and send it for you.
- [Custom limits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/llm/guides/custom-limits): Your own limits in code: $llm.onCall runs before every model call and can change it or refuse it, $llm.onCallDone runs after with what it cost. Plan tiers, credits, a model per plan and team buckets.

## Pages: Introduction

- [Overview of Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/overview): Pages is server-rendered multi-page apps for PocketOne, from a pb_pages folder of ETS templates, TypeScript and Markdown files.
- [Moving from PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/moving-from-0x): What changed between the PocketPages npm package (0.x) and Pages in PocketOne.
- [Coding agents](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/agents): Teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding agents Pages with the pocketone Agent Skill and llms.txt.

## Pages: Getting Started

- [Installation](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/installation): Run Pages on PocketOne with the pages extension, using a pb_pages folder.
- [Starter Kits](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/starter-kits): Start a new PocketOne app from a starter kit with pocketone pages create.

## Pages: Basics

- [Creating a Page](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/creating-a-page): Create .ets and .md files in pb_pages to add pages, with index files and nested folders mapping to URLs.
- [Directory Structure](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/directory-structure): How a pb_pages folder is organized, and the special +, _, - and . prefixes.
- [File types](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/file-types): Which file extensions Pages runs, the two template styles (ETS and TSX), and the JavaScript versions that work the same way.
- [Routing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/routing): How files in pb_pages map to URLs: pages, page code and endpoints (.ts), [param] segments, groups, static files, and which route wins.
- [Accessing Parameters](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/parameters): Read route parameters from [param] file and folder names with ctx.params, and query strings with ctx.req.query().
- [Loading Data](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/loading-data): Load data inline in templates or in the page's own .ts file with load and per-method handlers.
- [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/api-routes): Serve JSON and other non-HTML responses from a .ts file with no template, and ctx.res.json.

## Pages: Templating

- [ETS templates](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ets): An .ets file is HTML with TypeScript in EJS tags. The tags, escaping, what's in scope, and await.
- [Markdown](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/markdown): .md pages and partials run their tags as plain JavaScript, then Markdown, with YAML front matter passed to meta().
- [Partials](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/partials): Include reusable templates from _private folders with include(name, locals).
- [Layouts and Slots](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/layouts): Wrap pages with +layout.ets files, and pass content between pages and layouts with named slots.
- [Components with TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsx): The component style, with pages, layouts and partials as .tsx functions that return markup, rendered to HTML on the server with no build step.

## Pages: Security and Content

- [Private files](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/private-files): How _private folders hold partials and TypeScript modules for include() and ctx.resolve(), and which names are never routed.
- [Middleware](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/middleware): +middleware.ts files run root first for every route below them, with one (ctx, next) signature.
- [Asset Management](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/asset-management): Static files in pb_pages get content-hashed URLs through asset() for long-term caching.
- [Static content](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/static-content): Files in pb_pages that aren't pages or framework files are served as-is, with content types and ETags.
- [Managing Secrets](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/secrets): Read API keys and other secrets from environment variables with ctx.env().

## Pages: Configuration

- [+config.ts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/config): Turn on built-in plugins, add custom plugins, and enable debug output from pb_pages/+config.ts.
- [Caching](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/caching): How Pages caches templates, static files and fingerprinted assets.
- [Errors](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/errors): How Pages turns thrown errors into responses, ctx.httpError(), and custom +error and +404 pages.
- [Debugging](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/debugging): Dev mode, debug in +config.ts, and logging with ctx.log.
- [Going Live](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/deploying): Deploy a PocketOne app by putting pb_pages next to pb_data on a PocketOne server (pages is built in).

## Pages: Plugins

- [Overview](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins): Built-in plugins (auth, realtime) and custom plugins such as the Datastar add-on, turned on in +config.ts.
- [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/auth): The built-in auth plugin keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie and adds ctx.session sign-in methods.
- [Datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/datastar): The Datastar add-on adds ctx.datastar helpers for Datastar script tags, SSE patches and signals.
- [Realtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/realtime): The built-in realtime plugin sends messages to PocketBase realtime subscribers with ctx.realtime.send().
- [Authoring](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/plugins/authoring): Write a custom plugin for Pages, a factory that returns onRequest, extendContext and transform hooks.

## Pages: ctx Reference

- [Overview](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx): Reference for ctx, the one object per request passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.
- [req](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/req): The request - method, URL, query parameters, headers, cookies, body, uploaded files and client IP.
- [res](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/res): The response - status, headers, cookies, redirects with flash messages, JSON, HTML, text, files and server-sent events.
- [data, params, route](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/data): The shared data object, route parameters and the matched route.
- [flash](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/flash): One-time messages carried across a redirect in a cookie.
- [auth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/auth): The authenticated record for the request, or null.
- [app](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/app): The app - records, collections and settings.
- [pb (JS SDK)](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/pb): Query your app with the PocketBase JS SDK from page code, as the signed-in user.
- [env](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/env): Read environment variables.
- [log](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/log): Write to the app's log with debug, info, warn and error.
- [meta](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/meta): A per-request key/value store for page metadata such as title and description.
- [asset](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/asset): Content-hashed URLs for static files in pb_pages.
- [resolve](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/resolve): Load a module or file from a _private folder.
- [store](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/ctx/store): The app's in-memory store, shared across requests.

## Pages: Going Further

- [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/jsvm): Where page code runs, what it can reach, and using npm packages from pb_pages/node_modules.
- [TypeScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/typescript): Type-check page code against ctx, handlers, middleware, +config, plugins and JSX components, with the types PocketOne writes for your app.

## Pages: Guides

- [Authentication](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/authentication): Sign users in and out with the auth plugin - passwords, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sessions.
- [Realtime Events](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/realtime): Send realtime messages from pages with the realtime plugin, and receive them in the browser with the PocketBase JS SDK.
- [Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages/speedruns/gs-gmail): Complete walkthrough for configuring email domains in Google Suite, including domain verification, Gmail activation, catch-all email setup, MX record configuration, and sender account integration.

## Starter kits: Kits

- [Ask](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/ask): Ask your docs a question and get a short answer with links to the pages it came from.
- [Auth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/auth): Multi-page app (MPA) auth with the built-in `auth` plugin: register, password, anonymous, OTP and OAuth2 login, logout, email verification (with a resend page), password reset by email, email change with confirmation, and a protected `/account` section (`account/+middleware.ts`).
- [DaisyUI](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/daisyui): A layout with a responsive navbar and drawer, built with [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) and [DaisyUI](https://daisyui.com/) (cupcake theme).
- [DaisyUI docs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/daisyui-docs): A docs site built from Markdown pages, styled with [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) and [DaisyUI](https://daisyui.com/).
- [Datastar](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/datastar): A realtime chat with rooms and a live counter, built with [Datastar](https://data-star.dev/) and the Datastar add-on (`_private/datastar.js`, listed as `'datastar'`) and the built-in `realtime` plugin.
- [htmx](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/htmx): A realtime demo with [htmx](https://htmx.org/) and the built-in `realtime` plugin.
- [Minimal](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/minimal): A single `index.ets` page: a Tailwind (CDN) splash screen with no layout, no config and no build step.
- [MVP.css](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/mvp): One page styled with [MVP.css](https://andybrewer.github.io/mvp/): classless CSS that makes plain semantic HTML look good, for a minimal, responsive, mobile-friendly site with no build step.
- [TSX](https://pocketone.dev/docs/starters/tsx): Server-rendered components: a `+layout.tsx`, an `index.tsx` page built from a `_private/Feature.tsx` component, and `index.ts` beside it, which loads the page's data.

## WASM: Languages

- [Choosing a language](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages): Which languages build WASM modules for your app, what each one costs per call, and how to pick.
- [C and C++](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/c): Build a WASM module for your app from C or C++ with zig cc, which brings its own WASI libc.
- [Go](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/go): Build a WASM module for your app with Go's own compiler (GOOS=wasip1), and when its size matters.
- [TinyGo](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/tinygo): Build Go code into small, fast WASM modules for your app with TinyGo.
- [Rust](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/rust): Build WASM modules for your app from Rust, and use crates from crates.io in them.
- [Zig](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/zig): Build small WASM modules for your app with Zig.
- [AssemblyScript](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/assemblyscript): Build a WASM module for your app in AssemblyScript, a TypeScript-like language, with the WASI shim.
- [WebAssembly text (WAT)](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/wat): Write a WASM module for your app by hand in WebAssembly's own text format, calling WASI directly, with no compiler and no libc.
- [LLVM IR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/llvm): Write a WASM module for your app in LLVM IR, the assembly language compilers hand to LLVM, and let clang build it.
- [Other languages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/languages/others): What another language needs to build a WASM module your app can run, and how the usual candidates fit.

## WASM: Guides

- [Keeping state in JS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/guides/state): Modules keep nothing between calls. Keep the state in the app (a record, or $app.store()), pass it in with each call, and save what comes back. With a TinyGo example.

## WASM: Recipes

- [Overview](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes): WASM modules built on real libraries, each with page code that calls it: Markdown, HTML sanitizing, QR codes, thumbnails, diffs, CSV, EDIFACT and XML orders, and crypto JS lacks.
- [Markdown to HTML](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes/markdown): Render Markdown posts to HTML in page code with pulldown-cmark, then clean them with sanitize-html.
- [Sanitize HTML](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes/sanitize-html): Clean untrusted HTML from users with ammonia, so it's safe to show on your pages.
- [Text diffs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes/diff): Keep a revision history of a text field as unified diffs, with the similar crate.
- [Image thumbnails](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes/thumbnail): Make a PNG thumbnail of an uploaded photo in page code, with the image crate.
- [QR codes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes/qrcode): Draw a QR code as SVG for a ticket, a check-in link or a Wi-Fi login, with the qrcode crate.
- [CSV import](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm/recipes/csv): Import records from a CSV file, quoted fields and all, with the csv crate.

## Optional

- [PocketBase compatibility](https://pocketone.dev/docs/compatibility): Live results of PocketBase's own test suite, unmodified, run against PocketOne's core on every core change and daily.
- [Bedtime Story](https://pocketone.dev/docs/examples/bedtime-story): One topic told slowly and in depth, read aloud with pictures and music - the six steps, the player, the guards and the tuning screen in the dashboard.
- [New in PocketOne](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features): Everything PocketOne adds to PocketBase, side by side with what PocketBase gives you. All built into the pocketone binary.
- [Pages: sites in TSX, TypeScript or EJS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/features/sites): Server-rendered pages in TSX, JSX, TypeScript, EJS or Markdown, straight from a pb_pages folder next to your data. esbuild is built in, so there's no Node, no npm install and no build step.
- [Advanced installation](https://pocketone.dev/docs/guides/advanced-installation): Install PocketOne off the usual path - the install script's settings, Windows without Scoop, a release zip, or building it from source.
- [Authentication API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/authentication): Sign in to an auth collection over HTTP with a password, a one-time code or OAuth2, refresh tokens, verify emails, reset passwords, change emails and impersonate users.
- [Backups API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/backups): Make, list, download, upload, delete and restore backups of the app's pb_data over HTTP - for superusers.
- [Batch API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/batch): Send several record creates, updates and deletes in one request, run in one transaction - all of them happen, or none.
- [Collections API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/collections): Create, change, delete and import collections over HTTP - the endpoints the dashboard uses, for superusers.
- [Crons API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/crons): List the app's scheduled jobs and run one now - for superusers.
- [Files API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/files): Download a record's files and image thumbnails, and get short-lived tokens for protected files.
- [Health API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/health): Check whether the app is up, for load balancers, uptime monitors and deploy scripts.
- [Logs API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/logs): List, filter and read the app's request and app logs, and count them by hour - for superusers.
- [Realtime API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/realtime): Subscribe to record changes over server-sent events - connect, choose collections or single records, pass a filter, and get each create, update and delete as it happens.
- [Records API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/records): List, view, create, update and delete a collection's records over HTTP, with filters, sorting, paging, expanded relations, field selection and file uploads.
- [Settings API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/settings): Read and change the app's settings over HTTP - application, mail, files storage, backups, rate limits, logs and batch - and send test emails and S3 checks. For superusers.
- [SQL API](https://pocketone.dev/docs/rest/sql): Run a SQL statement against the app's database over HTTP and get columns and rows back - for superusers.
